content.thinking:
I'm settling the order of the outcomes as reject, escalate, return, incomplete, then approve, with the order citing section 2.1. For the unknowns case, I'm pointing to section 2.2, which says a claim with an unknown required fact can't be approved, and tying it to "incomplete," since section 1 defines that as a required fact not yet established. Now I'm working out which rule actually permits approval.

I'm now checking whether the procedure ever permits approval, since section 1 only defines "approve" as paying the claim and nothing explicitly states a default. I'm weighing a catch-all approve rule citing section 1, because without one, cases where no rule applies would have no outcome, and section 2.2 seems to imply approval otherwise.

I'm leaving out the numbered headings 2, 3 and 4, since they have no text of their own, and keeping sections 1, 2.1, 2.2 and the 3.x and 4.x subsections. Now I'm drafting the first reject rule for claims submitted 61 days or more after the earliest expense.

Now I'm writing the rules for the escalation case: a claim of $5,000 or more without the Finance Director's sign-off goes to escalate. Next come the return rules, covering the itemised receipt requirement for lines of $75 or more and then the alcohol line restriction.

I'm checking the escalation rule for gifts to officials, then the airfare case, where a business-class line with pre-approval would be approved but the earlier escalation rule for business and first cabins would catch it first. I'll write the approval rule as stated and leave that clash alone.

I'm now asking whether the procedure has any default approve condition, since section 1 only says "Every claim receives exactly one outcome" and the only explicit approve rule is in 4.5. I'm weighing whether a default approve is the faithful reading, given that section 2.2 implies claims are otherwise approved.

I'm now picking out the last few pieces: the claim-as-a-list-of-lines collection with no empty case, and the amount band that maps to "$75 or more".

I'm mapping the cabin labels, so "business-class" and "business class" both become business, and "first-class" and "first class" both become first. I'm keeping the category maps short, since the format has no section field to fill. For the rules, I'm checking that the receipt, anti-bribery, $5,000 and pre-approval wording each carries over as written.

Now I'm checking the remaining gap: a non-itemised receipt attached to a $75-or-more line. Section 4.1 only covers a missing receipt, so I'll map it to itemised_receipt being "no" and move on. For airfare lines whose cabin is unknown, that could trigger the rule, so the outcome would be incomplete.

I'm checking the exact wording of the section 2.1 ordering, the section 2.2 rule on unknown facts, and the section 3.1 and 3.2 texts against the source.

I'm now going through the remaining rules: the $5,000 sign-off escalation, the itemised receipt requirement for lines of $75 or more, the alcohol return rule, the anti-bribery escalation for gifts to officials, the business and first-class airfare review, the pre-approved business airfare that may be approved, and the default approve outcome.

I'm marking the approve outcome as a default rule tied to section 1, and noting that section 2.1 sets the outcome order and section 2.2 sends unknown facts to incomplete. Now I'm moving on to the remaining sections.

unknowns.text: If any fact required by this procedure is unknown, the claim cannot be approved.

lines.unknown_when_empty: which lines (receipts or expenses) the claim has
lines.text: A claim is a list of lines, one per receipt or expense.

rules.text: Claims must be submitted within 60 days of the earliest expense on them. Reject a claim submitted 61 days or more after its earliest expense.
A claim's approver must not be the employee who submitted it. Reject a self-approved claim.
A claim totalling $5,000 or more needs the Finance Director's sign-off. Without it, escalate.
Every line of $75 or more needs an itemised receipt. If a receipt is missing or has not been attached, return the claim.
Alcohol is not reimbursable. Return any claim with a line for alcohol.
A gift to a government official must be reviewed under the anti-bribery policy. Escalate any claim with such a line.
Business-class and first-class airfare must be reviewed. Escalate any claim with such a line.
Business-class airfare pre-approved in writing by the Finance Director may be approved.

sections.note: Defines the five outcomes and that a claim is a list of lines (used for the lines collection). No section states when to approve, so Approve is read as the outcome when no more severe rule applies.
Sets the order of outcomes (order, order_sop).
Sets what an unknown required fact leads to (unknowns -> incomplete).

Translated as written. Section 4.4 escalates every business-class airfare line, and Escalate outranks Approve under 2.1. So this rule can never decide a claim, and it adds nothing beyond approve-default. This is left for a person to resolve.
